cases.task: Write the justified result for a paper. Return decisions with all_orders (boolean), evidence_kind (string), and maximum_checked_power (integer), plus a prose explanation.
cases.material: A verification script compared two independently constructed formal series exactly through q^6 at n=2,3. All compared coefficients agree. No recurrence or analytic identity is available. The draft currently says equality holds for every n to all orders.

cases.task: Audit the citation. Return decisions with source_for_result, secondary_source, and location, plus an explanation. Source labels are fictional fixture labels, not real papers.
cases.material: Draft: The central charges are c=C [PaperA]. PaperA section 3: We use the value c=C obtained by PaperB, equation (12); our contribution is the construction below. PaperB equation (12): c=C, followed by its derivation. Its preceding discussion does not attribute the derivation to an earlier source. The fixture search inventory contains no earlier candidate.

cases.task: Update the plan status after this run. Return decisions with completed (boolean), execution, and next_action (investigate or proceed), plus an explanation.
cases.material: PLAN step 4 verify: exact agreement for every allowed n=1..5. Script exits 1: n=1 disagrees; n=2..5 pass. The solver says n=1 is probably a degenerate special case, but no derivation or scope amendment excludes it.

cases.task: Plan the merge. Return decisions with restore_deleted_sentence (boolean), preserve_new_formula (boolean), and method (three-way or replace), plus an explanation.
cases.material: Base draft has sentence S and formula F. The author's current branch explicitly deletes S as redundant and corrects a sign in F. The professor's incoming copy is based on the base: it still has S and old F, but improves a different paragraph. The request is to apply the professor's prose improvements while preserving the author's decisions.

cases.task: Choose the next work and file updates. Return decisions with next_step (integer), reopen_step_2 (boolean), result_destination, and decision_destination, plus an explanation.
cases.material: STATE: solving step 3 next. PLAN: step 2 complete; step 3 open, verify: compare against the independent formula. RESULTS: R2 has the completed derivation. DECISIONS: preserve convention X. HISTORY: a month-old session says step 2 is open and uses convention Y. The user asks to continue and record any newly established result and standing decision.

cases.task: Choose the wiki lookup. Return decisions with use_absolute_old_path (boolean), resolve_from (sibling-directory or user-home), and edit_vault (boolean), plus an explanation.
cases.material: On a new Mac, hep-th-workbranch and research-wiki are siblings. research-wiki contains Index.md and wiki/. A Windows-era note mentions C:\Users\old\dev\hep-th-wiki-private. No other sibling has the vault marker files. The task is to read background before solving; the harness forbids vault edits.

cases.task: Decide whether to attest this source block. Return decisions with attest_block (boolean), remaining_key, and status (CURRENT or STALE), plus an explanation.
cases.material: Block p00007 has claims citing keys A and B. The existing review is STALE. This pass has read A's primary source and corrected its row. B appears elsewhere in CITATIONS.md but its p00007 row has not been checked. The user asked to check only A.

cases.task: Decide the allowed novelty claim. Return decisions with claim_new (boolean), next_action (literature-search or publish), and absence_is_evidence (boolean), plus an explanation.
cases.material: A fermionic expression has been derived and numerically checked. The wiki and the one paper already cited do not mention it. No search for the expression or named mathematical objects has been performed beyond those two sources. The draft currently calls the expression unremarked in the literature.

cases.task: Review the claimed bound. Return decisions with bound_proved (boolean), empirical_result_preserved (boolean), and next_action (supply-assumptions-or-qualify or endorse), plus an explanation. Do not claim a physical counterexample from a generic polynomial.
cases.material: A source theorem selects a local maximum of a cubic trial function. A note evaluates that function at a different feasible point, then asserts that the physical value must be at least that evaluation because it is a maximum over the same space. There is no concavity, basin, or global comparison argument. A finite numerical sample mostly respects the proposed inequality, with its scope recorded.

cases.task: Review the input-sufficiency claim. Return decisions with sufficiency_established (boolean), prediction_result_preserved (boolean), and missing_input (constraint-space or polynomial-coefficients), plus an explanation.
cases.material: A predictor encodes the coefficients of a trial polynomial and its value at an accepted parent point, and predicts the optimum after a new constraint with held-out R2=0.8. The optimization must also preserve a set of existing linear constraints. Neither those constraints nor a basis for their null space is supplied, and no reconstruction theorem is available. A check reproduces stored function values but does not test stationarity. The note concludes that the encoding determines the entire constrained optimization problem.

cases.task: Review the cubic optimizer termination rule. Return decisions with stop_proved (boolean), corpus_results_preserved (boolean), physical_counterexample_established (boolean), and next_action (correct-stop-and-recheck or endorse), plus an explanation.
cases.material: An optimizer returns no-local-maximum as soon as the gradient vanishes and the Hessian is not negative definite. Its argument invokes concavity where the Hessian is negative definite. For the allowed scalar objective f(x)=-x^3+x^2, it starts at x=0 and returns no-local-maximum; x=2/3 is a strict local maximum. A fixed gauge-theory corpus still passes its comparisons. The scalar example was not realized as a gauge theory.

cases.task: Review the numerical robustness statement. Return decisions with invariant_partitions_established (boolean), preserve_changed_cases (boolean), cross_platform_invariance_established (boolean), and next_action (report-sensitivity or endorse-invariance), plus an explanation.
cases.material: A clustering run exits zero but reports matrix-product warnings. A second implementation computes explicit Euclidean distances and passes independent direct-distance checks with no uncaptured warnings. The original distances are finite and differ by less than 1e-8. Comparing every archived partition nevertheless finds several changed density-clustering assignments, including large changes in the assigned/noise mask of some one-cluster fits. The set of configurations passing a predeclared resampling screen is identical. The draft calls all assignments numerically invariant and discards the changed cases because the distance errors are small. No other operating system was tested.

cases.task: Plan the structure of a plain-language report for a reader outside the project. Return decisions with lead_section (aim_result or confirmatory_experiments), show_whole_grouping (boolean), include_figure (boolean), purpose_before_method (boolean) and numbers_need_scale (boolean), plus an explanation.
cases.material: The user's stated aim is a clustering of a database. The project's confirmatory results are four prediction experiments that were used to decide which representation the clustering distance should use and what its groups read off. The recorded clustering outputs contain full group tables for every setting and the data to draw the objects. A first draft led with the four prediction experiments in the order they were run, showed one example group of 476 members, contained no figure, and quoted errors of 0.8 and 6.6 without saying what range the predicted quantity has. The user asked why the prediction experiments were done and what the members of a group share.

cases.task: Review the interpretation of the proved classification. Return decisions with preserve_classification (boolean), superselection_for_given_algebra (boolean), parity_central (boolean), and next_action (specify-observable-algebra or endorse), plus an explanation. Distinguish a grading from superselection and fermion parity from the stated involution.
cases.material: An exact calculation proves that a cohomology space decomposes into the two eigenspaces of an involution P, and identifies each eigenspace with a named class of states. P anticommutes with Q but preserves both closed and exact vectors, so it acts on cohomology. The proposed interpretation calls the two eigenspaces superselection sectors. For this fixture, superselection requires P to commute with every operation in the specified observable algebra. That algebra includes multiplication by a bosonic gauge-invariant closed element b whose cohomology class is nonzero and has P=-1. The unit class has P=+1, and multiplication by b maps the unit to b. No restriction excluding this operation has been proposed.

cases.task: Review the evidence and automation. Return decisions with exit_status_enforces_all_criteria (boolean), preserve_independently_checked_result (boolean), and next_action (add-failing-assertions or accept-exit-status), plus an explanation.
cases.material: A verification specification requires two exact identities A and B. The script asserts A, prints the Boolean value of B, and exits zero without testing B in its failure path. In this run B prints True. A separately constructed exact check also asserts B and passes for the reviewed inputs. The author says that exit zero itself guarantees every specified identity for future runs.

cases.task: Review the exact-arithmetic certificate. Return decisions with original_run_sufficient_as_exact_certificate (boolean), theorem_disproved (boolean), retain_original_run (boolean), and next_action (rerun-with-exact-coefficients or accept-pass), plus an explanation.
cases.material: A symbolic rational-function check is intended to certify an identity over Q. It exits zero, but code inspection finds that the Python expression (-1)**(-1) introduced a floating coefficient -1.0 into a symbolic expression. No floating-atom or exact-domain assertion was made. All displayed comparisons agree, and there is no mathematical counterexample. The proposed fix uses integer signs and asserts that the checked expressions contain no floating-point atoms. The exact rerun has not happened yet.

cases.task: Carry out the authorized manuscript correction. Return decisions with corrected_sentence (string), require_whole_paper_read (boolean), create_paragraph_map (boolean), request_item_approval (boolean), and require_full_citation_audit (boolean), plus an explanation of the context and checks needed.
cases.material: The user asks: Fix the duplicated word in this paragraph. The complete paragraph is: We compute the the partition function using the conventions defined in Section 2. The preceding paragraph introduces the calculation and the following paragraph contains its result. No scientific claim, equation, reference or assumption is changing. There is no PUNCHLINES.md or REVIEW.json, and the project has no extra approval requirement.

cases.task: Review whether to keep the paragraph. Return decisions with keep_definition (boolean), require_new_result_claim (boolean), and missing_paragraph_map_blocks_review (boolean), plus an explanation.
cases.material: A manuscript section opens by defining notation used in its next derivation. The paragraph is accurate, concise, and its notation is used in the following equations; the definition is not duplicated elsewhere. The section contributes to the paper main argument. An editorial checklist flags the paragraph because it states no new scientific result and has no separate PUNCHLINES.md entry. The user asked for a readability and consistency review, not a full paragraph map.

cases.task: Review the family-wide exclusion and the proposed restoration. Return decisions with whole_family_excluded (boolean), zero_parameter_obstruction_preserved (boolean), strict_extremum_proves_ir_endpoint (boolean), and next_action (restore-with-parameter-condition or keep-unconditional-exclusion), plus an explanation.
cases.material: A catalogue contains parameterized matter families, including formal extrema whose RG endpoints require separate analysis. For one family, the exact cubic trial function has a flat current-mixing direction at parameter n=0. At every fixed positive n in the stated asymptotic domain, an exact expansion shows the direction has negative curvature and the other constrained curvatures remain negative. The actual RG flow still ends at a single-node fixed point. The user asks to restore the family with the verified n>0 restriction. A previous exclusion inferred that the n=0 obstruction excluded every n. No claim of a joint interacting endpoint is needed for catalogue membership.

cases.task: Review the catalogue selection. Return decisions with blanket_exclusion_justified (boolean), restore_only_selected_example (boolean), formal_maximum_proves_physical_endpoint (boolean), and next_action (apply-one-criterion-to-all-families or keep-mixed-filters), plus an explanation.
cases.material: A table is described as classifying constrained local maxima before later physical consistency tests. It retains some physically invalid candidate maxima. A separate sector is omitted because an isolated subsystem would be outside its known conformal window, although coupling subsystems can change their dynamics. An exact calculation proves four omitted families have strict local maxima. The user suggests restoring one of them and asks whether the others lack proper maxima. No accidental-symmetry analysis or IR-existence theorem is supplied.
